what: a modelled M3x0.2 thread in a 3 mm hole drawn at the thread's nominal size (was refused like any hole at the nominal size)
method: ISO 68-1 basic profile: H = P sqrt3/2, basic depth 5H/8. External groove (the space between teeth): a trapezoid P/4 wide at the root radius d/2 - 5H/8, widening by 2 tan30 per unit of radius to 7P/8 at d/2. Internal groove: P/8 wide at the major radius d/2, widening to 3P/4 at the minor radius, cut only where there is material (r >= hole radius). Pappus: volume per turn = 2 pi A rc (A the trapezoid area, rc its centroid radius from the axis); a helical sweep of L/P turns removes exactly (L/P) x that, where each end of the thread is a free end or lies inside material. A 3 mm hole through a D10 x 2 disc, drawn at the thread's nominal size, takes a modelled M3x0.2: the hole is first filled to the tap drill (major - pitch = 2.8 mm, rho=1.4), then the groove is cut, the same thread as in a hole drilled at the tap drill. Whole length, both ends free (10 turns): V = pi 5^2 2 - pi 1.4^2 2 - 10 x V_turn(clipped at rho) = 157.0796 - 12.3150 - 10 x 0.07477 = 144.0169 mm3. The thin lips a tap leaves at each end are below 0.2% of the volume. Tolerance 1%: a modelled thread is a faceted helical solid (radial chord error up to 1% of the pitch on every wall, i.e. a volume deficit of about 4/3 x sag/R).
